probes.support_reason: F-1: all three numbered sub-requirements are delivered - (1) the C standard-library function `int abs(int)` is declared as a foreign function with Quidra's own built-in FFI form `extern int32 c_abs(int32 value) = "abs"` (int32 is the fixed-width type that matches C `int` on this target; the Quidra-side name must differ from `abs` only because `abs` is an absolutely reserved builtin identifier, and `c_abs` is the spelling the language reference's own FFI example uses), (2) it is called once with -3, and (3) the returned C int is bound to an int32 local and produced, value 3. F-2/F-4: no third-party package, no binding generator, no separate build step - `quidra build` alone, linking against the platform C library the frozen recipe already links. F-3: builds and prints 3. F-6: the FFI is documented as a first-class, deliberately narrow facility; no normative prohibition or deprecation sentence applies to it. Evidence that the declaration really binds the C symbol rather than being folded away in source: `quidra llvm` emits `declare i32 @abs(i32)` and `call i32 @abs(i32 %v2)` (the final -O3 binary constant-folds the call to the literal 3, which is an optimization of the linked call, not a substitution of it).
